# Motorola Edge (2026) now available in the US and Canada

 Michail 12 June 2026 

Following its announcement last week, the Motorola Edge (2026) is now on open sale in the US and Canada.

In the US, the 6.3-inch OLED flaunting Dimensity 7450-powered device can be had for $600 unlocked from Motorola.com as well as partnering retailers like BestBuy. That’s for the single 128GB storage trim in the Pantone Martini Olive color.

Motorola US is bundling a free pair of Moto Buds Loop and a Moto Watch with early orders

Early buyers are eligible for a free pair of Moto Buds Loop and Moto Watch, which have a combined value of $400. This campaign will be limited while supplies last.

In Canada, the Edge (2026) is priced at CAD 850 for the same 128GB storage trim and Pantone Martini Olive color. For more details on the Edge (2026), check out our announcement news.

title: Motorola Edge 2026 Release Date
text:
# Motorola Edge 2026 Release Date

Alexander Maxham | 

Jun 3, 2026

 

Motorola finally made it official. The Motorola Edge 2026 was announced on June 2, and it’s going on sale June 11 for $599. That’s a $50 bump over last year’s model, but honestly, given the current memory pricing chaos hitting the entire industry, that’s not surprising at all. And a smaller price bump over the Moto G models that were announced earlier this year.

If you’ve been waiting for Motorola’s North American mid-range pick of the year, mark your calendar. June 11 is the day. You’ll be able to grab it unlocked from Best Buy and Motorola.com, and Verizon is also getting it on launch day. AT&T, Cricket Wireless, Spectrum Wireless, and Xfinity Mobile are all picking it up afterward, so coverage isn’t going to be an issue here.

### What you’re actually getting for $599

This $599 price point is pretty competitive right now, especially when you look at what Motorola is packing into this thing. You’re getting a 6.3-inch Extreme AMOLED display that hits 5,200 nits peak brightness, which is genuinely wild for a phone at this tier. It’s also 120Hz, Pantone Validated, and runs at Super HD (2640 x 1216) resolution.

The processor is where things get a little less exciting. Motorola went with the MediaTek Dimensity 7450, which is the same chip used in the Razr 2025 and the original Razr 2024. It’s paired with 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage. Not flagship-tier, but it’ll get the job done.

...

Battery life looks solid, too. The 5,000mAh cell is rated for up to 50 hours, and you get 60W TurboPower wired charging plus 15W wireless. Toss in IP68/IP69 water resistance, MIL-STD-810H durability, Gorilla Glass 7i, and Android 16 out of the box, and there’s a lot to like.

...

This is just one piece of Motorola’s massive 2026 push. The company’s full Edge family for 2026 includes seven devices, with the Motorola Edge 70 Pro+ also launching this month. But for North American buyers who just want a solid, affordable Android phone, the Edge 2026 is the one to watch. June 11 can’t get here fast enough.

title: A thinner, lighter Motorola Edge 2026 has just popped up for pre-order
text:
# A thinner, lighter Motorola Edge 2026 has just popped up for pre-order

Credit: Motorola

 By Chandra Steele 

 Published Jun 2, 2026, 2:06 PM EDT 

Chandra Steele has been writing about tech for the entirety of her journalism career. She loves making tough topics easy to understand. Before joining Android Police, Chandra was senior features writer at PCMag where she did everything from interviewing Jeff Goldblum to explaining crypto. 

Motorola just announced that a very compact and light Motorola Edge 2026 in an unusual color is coming to the US on June 11, with pre-orders starting today.

## A smaller phone, a bold color choice 

The annual Motorola Edge drop has a 6.3-inch display, down from last year’s 6.7 inches and weighs just 160 grams, compared to the 2025’s 181 grams.

The display is a 2640×1216 AMOLED panel with a 120Hz refresh rate and peak brightness of 5,200 nits. Motorola has termed the display “Extreme AMOLED.” Like last year’s Edge, the display is covered by Gorilla Glass 7i.

There’s a MediaTek Dimensity 7450 chipset onboard, as well as 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage. The battery is 5,000mAh, and supports 60W fast wired charging and 15W wireless charging.

As for the cameras, there is one improvement over the 2025 model: a 50MP Sony Lytia 710 main rear sensor. Unchanged from last year is a 50MP ultrawide shooter, a 10MP 3x optical zoom camera, and a 50MP selfie camera.

The 2026 Motorola Edge is going for a sophisticated, British look. It comes in the Pantone shade Martini Olive and its back surface is meant to evoke a tweed pattern. It’s a departure from the crunchier-seeming 2025 model’s Pantone Deep Forest with a soft-touch vegan leather back.

One of the biggest leaps the Motorola Edge has made from last year is its price. It will sell for $599, a $50 increase.

title: Samsung’s Galaxy A57 and A37 finally match flagships where it matters most | Android Central

Samsung’s Galaxy A57 and A37 finally match flagships where it matters most | Android Central

# Samsung’s Galaxy A57 and A37 finally match flagships where it matters most

 By Jay Bonggolto 

 Published 25 March 2026 

Samsung’s new Galaxy A phones pack smarter features without flagship prices.

 (Image credit: Samsung) 

## What you need to know

- The Galaxy A57 and A37 pack Awesome Intelligence tools like transcription, AI text extraction, and smarter multitasking.
- Camera AI gets upgrades too, with better Object Eraser, improved group shots, and smarter visual search.
- Pricing starts at $450 for the A37 and $550 for the A57, with multiple color options and availability from April 9, 2026.

Flagship phones have hoarded the best AI features for years, forcing buyers to choose between having the smartest software and keeping their savings. Now, Samsung is changing things up. The new Galaxy A57 5G and Galaxy A37 5G bring a bunch of Awesome Intelligence tools to phones under $600.

...

Samsung is promising long-term support, with up to six Android OS upgrades and six years of security updates. Security features include Knox Vault, Auto Blocker, and Privacy Alerts that warn you about suspicious data monitoring.

The Galaxy A57 5G will be available in the U.S. starting April 9, 2026, with a price of $550. It comes unlocked in Awesome Navy from Samsung’s website and Experience Stores. The Galaxy A37 5G starts at $450 and is available in Awesome Charcoal or Awesome Lavender from Samsung. Best Buy will offer a Graygreen version, and Amazon will have an Awesome White option.

...

It’s impressive that Samsung is offering six years of OS and security updates, along with Awesome Intelligence tools, on phones under $600. For most people, this means you can keep a capable phone for five years without worrying about missing out on new AI features.

title: Motorola Edge 2026 Price
text:
Motorola Edge 2026 Price

# Motorola Edge 2026 Price

Alexander Maxham | 

Jun 3, 2026

 

Motorola has set the Motorola Edge 2026 price at $599, and it goes on sale June 11. That’s a $50 jump from last year’s model, which launched at $549. So the question on everyone’s mind is pretty simple. Is this phone actually worth $599, or is Motorola just riding the same wave of price hikes hitting every phone in 2026?

Here’s my take. $599 is still a solid price for what you’re getting. But the bump is worth talking about.

...

Unfortunately, every phone is going up in price this year. That’s not Motorola’s fault; that’s the worldwide RAM shortage problem. The current RAM shortage (some folks are calling it the “RAMpocalypse”) has driven component costs through the roof, and basically every Android OEM is passing those costs along to buyers. Samsung did it. Google did it. Motorola is doing it. So while the $50 increase over the Motorola Edge 2025 stings a bit, it’s honestly not that bad in context.

What I do want to point out, though, is that the 2026 model technically has less storage out of the box than last year’s version. The Edge 2025 came with 256GB standard. The Edge 2026 ships with 128GB. So you’re paying more for less storage, which is a little annoying. And it’s the same thing Motorola did with the Razr 2026 series a little over a month ago. 

The processor is also the same Dimensity 7450 used in the Razr 2025, so you’re not really getting a chipset upgrade either.

...

At $599, the Motorola Edge 2026 is going head-to-head with the Google Pixel 10a, which sits in the same price range. The Pixel has better software and AI features, but Motorola has a brighter display, a telephoto camera, and faster charging. Honestly, for a lot of buyers, that’s a tougher choice than you’d think.

If you want to wait for something else, the rest of Motorola’s 2026 Edge family includes seven devices, though most are international releases. The closest North American alternative will probably be whatever ends up replacing the Edge 70 Ultra here, but that’ll cost considerably more.

Bottom line, $599 is a fair price. Just don’t expect a massive leap over last year.

title: POCO F8 Pro Releases Globally with Snapdragon 8 Elite, HyperOS 3, & Huge Battery For Under $600 - Gizmochina
text:
POCO F8 Pro Releases Globally with Snapdragon 8 Elite, HyperOS 3, & Huge Battery For Under $600 - Gizmochina

# POCO F8 Pro Releases Globally with Snapdragon 8 Elite, HyperOS 3, & Huge Battery For Under $600

By

Sean

Nov 26, 2025

POCO has officially unveiled the POCO F8 Pro on the global stage. This device has just debuted worldwide, bringing high end specs and features for an approachable price tag. The company just announced the POCO F8 Ultra, alongside the F8 Pro, so here are all the details for the more affordable F8 model.

## POCO F8 Pro Global Launch: What does it offer?

The Chinese brand just announced the POCO F8 Pro with a 6.59-inch OLED display with a 1.5K resolution, a 120Hz refresh rate, and 3500 nits of peak brightness. Under the hood, this device is equipped with Qualcomm’s older flagship chip, the Snapdragon 8 Elite, which is coupled with 12GB of RAM and up to 512GB of internal storage. A gigantic 6,210mAh battery pack powers this device, which supports 100W wired fast charging. Notably, the POCO F8 Pro is basically a rebranded global version of the Redmi K90 that packs a larger 7,100mAh cell.

POCO F8 Pro

For optics, the rear has a 50MP Light Fusion main sensor (OIS, 1/1.55-inch) along with a 50MP telephoto shooter with a 2.5x optical zoom, and an 8MP ultra wide angle lens, while the front houses a 20MP shooter for selfies and video calls. Other notable features included WiFi 7, Liquid Cool technology for thermal management, Android 16 OS based HyperOS 3 custom skin out of the box, 22.5W reverse wired charging, an in-display fingerprint scanner, and an IP68 rating for water and dust resistance.

## Pricing and Availability

The brand just announced the POCO F8 Pro in three color options, namely Black, Blue, and Titanium Silver. It has a starting price tag of $579 for the 12GB + 256GB model, while the 12GB + 512GB version costs $629. Although, the brand is offering a $50 discount for both variants as a part of an introductory launch offer, which brings down its effective price to just $529. It is worth noting that the deal is available only till December 10.

title: Motorola Edge (2026) debuts with 6.3-inch display, 3x telephoto camera, and more
text:
# Motorola Edge (2026) debuts with 6.3-inch display, 3x telephoto camera, and more

By

Marcia Sekhose

 -

Published On: 3 June 2026 | 09:27 IST

Highlights

- Motorola Edge (2026) features a compact 6.3-inch display.
- It has a triple-camera setup with a telephoto lens.
- The smartphone could launch as Motorola Edge 70 Neo in other markets.

Motorola has unveiled the latest addition to its Edge lineup in North America, introducing the Motorola Edge (2026) as a feature-packed upper mid-range smartphone in a compact form factor. While the branding is specific to the US market, the Motorola Edge (2026) could eventually arrive in markets like India under a different name, potentially as the Motorola Edge 70 Neo, since the Neo lineup has a compact display among its siblings.

## Motorola Edge (2026) price

In the US, the Motorola Edge (2026) will go on sale from June 11th with a retail price of $599.99 (Rs 57,300 approx). Pricing will vary depending on the market. The device will be offered in a distinctive Pantone Martini Olive finish, featuring an earthy green-gold tone and a textured twill-inspired rear panel.

...

At the front, the phone features a compact 6.3-inch OLED 1.5K display with a 120Hz refresh rate, HDR10+ certification, and a peak brightness rating of 5,200 nits. The panel is further protected by Corning Gorilla Glass 7i. Despite a compact screen, you’re getting a vibrant and bright display, which should make the viewing and scrolling experience highly pleasing.

Powering the device is MediaTek’s Dimensity 7450 chipset, built on a 4nm process. The processor is paired with 8GB of LPDDR5X RAM and 128GB of storage. The smartphone should be able to handle regular to moderate tasks with no hiccups. The Edge (2026) ships with Android 16 out of the box and comes with a commitment of three major Android OS upgrades.

title: Motorola Edge 2026 Packs Compact Style, 50MP Cameras, and Rugged Midrange Hardware - Tech ShowUp
text:
# Motorola Edge 2026 Packs Compact Style, 50MP Cameras, and Rugged Midrange Hardware

 Sunday, 14 June 2026 16:54 · 914 views By Michel K.

Motorola’s newest Edge trims the size, leans into durability, and mixes Android 16 with a camera setup aimed at users who want premium touches without an oversized flagship.

## A Smaller Edge Arrives in the U.S. 

As of Sunday, June 14, 2026, the Motorola Edge 2026 is now available in the U.S., following its June 11 release. The phone lands at $599.99 unlocked, putting it in the same midrange conversation as higher-end Pixel A-series, Galaxy A-series, and OnePlus alternatives rather than ultra-premium flagships. The bigger story is the shift in size: Motorola moved this Edge to a 6.3-inch form factor, making it noticeably more compact than last year’s larger Edge model. That gives the 2026 version a clearer identity for users who want a modern Android phone that does not feel oversized in a pocket or hand. (phonearena.com)

...

The front of the phone is a 6.3-inch Extreme AMOLED display with a 1.5K Super HD resolution, 120Hz refresh rate, and peak brightness listed at up to 5200 nits. Inside, Motorola uses the MediaTek Dimensity 7450 with 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage. Power comes from a 5000mAh battery, with support for 60W TurboPower wired charging and 15W wireless charging. Motorola also includes stereo speakers with Dolby Atmos, Bluetooth 5.4, NFC, USB-C, and Android 16 out of the box. The spec sheet is not trying to chase gaming-phone extremes, but it covers the features many people expect from a $600 Android phone in 2026. (motorola.com) View Google Pixel 10 on partner website

...

Motorola promotes the Edge 2026 around triple 50MP cameras plus a telephoto lens, but the actual layout is worth spelling out. The phone has a 50MP Sony LYTIA main camera, a 50MP ultrawide camera, a 50MP selfie camera, and a separate 10MP telephoto camera with 3x optical zoom and up to 30x Super Zoom. That means the rear camera system is not three 50MP sensors; instead, the 50MP theme spans the main, ultrawide, and front cameras. It is still a flexible setup for the class, especially because the dedicated telephoto lens gives users an optical zoom option that many midrange phones skip. (motorola.com) Explore Google Pixel 9 Pro as a camera-focused alternative

...

On the software side, the Edge 2026 ships with Android 16 and Motorola’s newer AI features, including moto ai and Google Gemini support. Motorola’s official product page also mentions two guaranteed Android OS upgrades, which is useful to know because longer update policies have become a bigger factor for buyers comparing Android phones. The main trade-offs are straightforward: storage is listed at 128GB, the charger is not the headline feature it once was, and the price is higher than some previous Edge models. Still, the Edge 2026 has a clear angle: a compact Android phone with a bright display, rugged ratings, wireless charging, and a camera mix that aims for practical flexibility rather than flagship bragging rights.
